name: Signal
description: Signal is a private messenger for end-to-end encrypted text, voice messages, photos, files, stories, group conversations and voice or video calls across mobile and linked desktop devices. It minimizes service metadata, stores readable conversation history on a person's devices and gives each linked device its own encryption keys.
agentUseSummary: Signal cannot be connected to Relay agents because Signal publishes no supported OAuth, account API, bot platform or remote MCP service. Official Desktop and iPad linking is an interactive QR-provisioning flow that creates a full trusted device with conversation keys, while Signal's terms prohibit auto-messaging, bulk messaging, automated accounts and unauthorized collection; protocol libraries and unofficial CLIs are not acceptable personal-account authority.

blocked.label: Connect or register Signal
blocked.description: Relay cannot register a phone number, receive a verification code, scan a linked-device QR code or provision itself as a trusted Signal device.

blocked.label: Read or export conversations
blocked.description: Messages, attachments, contacts, groups, stories, call history, receipts, profiles, usernames, keys and backups cannot be read, searched, synchronized, exported or disclosed to agents.

blocked.label: Send or manage messages
blocked.description: Agents cannot send, reply, react, edit, delete, forward, schedule, mark read, manage disappearing messages, administer groups or change account and privacy settings.

blocked.label: Make or manage calls
blocked.description: Voice and video calling, group calls, ringing, answering, call links, media, screen sharing and call controls are unavailable.

blocked.label: Automate or bulk message
blocked.description: Automated accounts, auto-messaging, auto-dialing, bulk messaging, unsolicited communication, scraping and unauthorized collection are blocked by Relay and Signal's acceptable-use terms.

blocked.label: Use unofficial or private access
blocked.description: Unofficial CLIs, reverse-engineered service endpoints, repurposed Signal Desktop databases, decrypted backups, UI scripting, verification-code capture and raw libsignal or Signal-Server calls are never accepted.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No Signal action is enabled because Signal provides no supported third-party account or bot API and Relay will not become an automated linked client.

runtimeSupport.description: No Signal tools are mounted because Signal exposes no supported automation API and a runtime cannot inherit a person's device registration, linked-device keys or encrypted conversation authority.

providerSetup.blocker: Signal accounts require a primary Android, iPhone or separately registered iPad associated with a phone number. Official linked devices are Signal Desktop or linked iPad clients that a person provisions by scanning a QR code from the primary phone; each obtains its own keys and access to private communications, and may receive synchronized chat history and recent media. Signal publishes open-source clients, server code and libsignal cryptographic libraries for transparency and its own implementations, but no supported third-party personal-account, bot or automation contract. Its terms prohibit bulk messaging, auto-messaging, auto-dialing, automated account creation, unauthorized service access and unauthorized user-data collection. Relay has no lawful bounded scope, supported credential boundary or safe way to turn a full linked device into per-agent capabilities.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not ask for a phone number, verification code, PIN, recovery key, linked-device QR scan, backup key or Signal Desktop data. Do not install or wrap signal-cli, link Relay as a device, automate the official clients or call private service endpoints. Keep Signal unavailable unless Signal publishes a supported distributable developer or bot API with bounded scopes and terms permitting agent automation, or grants Relay written authorization for an exact reviewed client contract; then design read and communication capabilities separately, require approval for external communication in Safe mode, preserve disappearing-message semantics and verify revocation and device unlinking.

evidence.supports: Signal describes private encrypted messaging and calling on registered mobile clients and states that Signal Desktop must be linked to Signal on Android or iPhone.
Signal requires a mobile app, an existing phone number and an SMS or voice verification code for primary registration and warns users not to share that code.
Signal supports user-present QR linking only for Signal Desktop or iPad, limits linked devices and lets the person choose whether to synchronize chats and recent media.
Signal explains that each linked device receives unique encryption keys through primary-device-approved provisioning and that readable history exists on personal devices rather than Signal's service.
Signal describes libsignal as protocol and cryptographic primitives used by its official clients and servers and says published packages are for Signal's own use, not a hosted account API.
Signal publishes official client, server, calling and protocol source code for transparency, but the organization exposes no supported third-party bot or personal-account SDK.
Signal's terms prohibit bulk messaging, auto-messaging, auto-dialing, automated account creation, unauthorized access and unauthorized collection of information about users.
